prospects.thesis: CACI is a pure-play defense IT and intelligence contractor with deep exposure to signals intelligence, cyber, and electronic warfare programs — all priority areas in the current DoD budget environment. At 1.5x P/S with a $13.9B cap and +26.7% 1M momentum, it offers institutional-quality growth at a reasonable multiple relative to hyperscaler-adjacent AI names. Bullish institutional flow plus continued defense budget tailwinds create a favorable setup.

UiPath is the leading enterprise RPA/agentic automation platform, now pivoting hard into AI agents where it has a natural distribution advantage into Fortune 500 back offices. Top composite score, bullish options flow, and bullish institutional positioning suggest smart money is anticipating a re-rating as agentic AI monetization accelerates. At 4.6x P/S and only a $7.6B cap, it's a reasonably valued mid-cap AI play with asymmetric upside.

Broadcom is the dominant custom silicon (ASIC) partner for hyperscalers building AI accelerators, plus its VMware integration is now driving margin expansion. Bullish options flow and institutional support align with Technology being the hottest sector (+6.99% 5D). With NVDA already on the watchlist, AVGO offers complementary exposure to the custom-silicon side of the AI infrastructure buildout.

GitLab is a full-stack DevSecOps platform with GitLab Duo (AI coding assistant) directly competing with GitHub Copilot, giving it a clear AI monetization vector via seat upsell. At 6.5x P/S and $6.6B cap, it's meaningfully cheaper than peers while showing bullish options and institutional signals with strong +19.3% momentum. The AI-native developer tools category remains one of the highest-conviction software sub-themes.

RTX offers diversified defense exposure across missile systems (Raytheon), advanced avionics (Collins), and propulsion (Pratt & Whitney), with the GTF engine issues largely in the rearview and record backlog supporting multi-year revenue visibility. Bullish options flow and institutional support with a more measured +10% 1M gain suggest room to run without chasing extended momentum. Complements CACI by adding large-cap prime contractor exposure versus pure-play services.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Here's what jumps out: the smart money is aggressively piling into defensive and rate-sensitive sectors — Real Estate, Utilities, Staples, and Healthcare are seeing massive call buying, which is classic "risk-off" positioning that says big players expect the Fed to cut rates and/or the economy to slow. The Healthcare bid is especially loud (nearly 10x normal volume), which often front-runs Washington news — think drug pricing negotiations easing up, Medicare reimbursement clarity, or M&A deregulation under the current administration's lighter antitrust posture. Meanwhile, they're dumping or hedging the growth-and-consumer trade: Tech's put/call ratio at 14 is a screaming hedge against the AI-mega-cap complex, and Industrials/Consumer Discretionary getting sold likely reflects tariff anxiety — new trade measures raise input costs for manufacturers and squeeze household budgets, which hits Amazon, Tesla, and homebuilders directly. Historically, this exact rotation — defensives up, cyclicals and tech down, with credit spreads widening and junk bonds catching a weird bullish bid (probably a short squeeze or covering, not real conviction) — precedes a 5-10% correction or at minimum a choppy 1-2 months where the index masks serious damage under the hood. The contradiction worth noting: markets near highs while options desks position like a storm is coming — someone's wrong, and options traders usually aren't. The non-obvious read the headlines are missing: the Utilities call buying isn't just a rate-cut bet, it's an AI power-demand play colliding with defensive positioning — meaning institutions think you can hide from a tech selloff *inside* the tech story by owning the picks-and-shovels (power, data center REITs) rather than the chips
